status: Session draft for gate GSP10 (SP10 stalled peers); NOT registered, no measured run. Registration copies the plan and rule into gsp10-v1-plan.json / gsp10-v1-protocol.json with the source manifest, image ids and harness hashes, after the prerequisites below (harness ban counter, image, non-measurement wiring smoke).
item: SP10: C0 = today's defaults (edges start + upstream deadlines since gsp02-v4 PASS:C2; relay_stall_policy legacy) vs CW = the same + relay_stall_policy watchdog (every 0.5 s during an active stream: a peer with outstanding requests and no payload for 2 s, while another peer of the same torrent progressed, is put on the session ip_filter for 120 s).
supersedes_draft: The earlier stream-scoped piece_timeout candidate (C10) is withdrawn: G0 v2 showed it only moves the delay from piece 0 to the last piece (upstream/mixed 16 MiB edges 13.34 s with 2 s vs 11.82 s with today's 10 s).

basis.g0: docs/feature/stream-performance/evidence/g0-sp10-stalled-probe-v2.json (252 runs, 0 failed; raw libtorrent, synthetic swarm; not a measurement). upstream/mixed, time until both boundary pieces are done ('edges'), median [min-max]: 16 MiB ctrl 4.78 [4.78-6.83], two stalled peers 11.82 [11.22-12.30], probe watchdog 6.34 [6.30-7.62] (n=3), keep-alive stalled peers + watchdog 6.35; 4 MiB ctrl 2.40, stalled 5.76, watchdog 4.05 [4.04-4.11]. 12 bans, 0 false; 0 bans without stalled peers.

gsp02_v4_mixed_means_C2.note: today's default start in the 8-peer mixed profile with 2 stalled peers, n=10 each; descriptive context, not part of this gate

prerequisites.harness_ban_counter: scripts/benchmark_sp_playback_controller.py must count the app log lines 'Relay stall watchdog: banned=<n> ...' into record['app_log']['stall_bans'] (sum of n), so the false-ban hard check is machine-readable. Not implemented in this session (the controller is shared with running gates); a small change with its own test before registration.
prerequisites.image: build stremhu-source:sp-cand-<commit> from the registered commit (both arms use the same image, they differ only in app_env)
prerequisites.wiring_smoke: Non-measurement: one CW run in mixed/16MiB/30Mbit with --only 1: the app log contains 'Relay stall watchdog: banned=' lines with banned >= 1; one C0 run: no such line. Also check there is no 'duplicate peer-id' disconnect (pb0-v2 seed containers each start their peer-id sequence at 1).

slowlive.why: no stalled peer, but slow and high-latency live peers: every ban here is a false ban

plan.runs: 13 cells x 2 arms x 10 = 260 runs; at the gsp02-v4 pace (~50 s per run) about 3.6 h

decision_rule.machine_rule: scripts/decide_sp_gate_bootstrap.py (sha256 at registration) plus the hard checks below
decision_rule.primary_metric: start.time_to_start_s (playback start: includes the TTFB, the parallel tail probe of the last piece and the 2 s buffer, i.e. waits for both boundary pieces)
decision_rule.pooling: both series pooled: n = 10 runs per arm and cell; failed runs excluded and counted
decision_rule.statistic: difference of means (CW - C0); 10 000 bootstrap resamples per test, fixed seed (set at registration); one-sided bootstrap p-values
decision_rule.improvement: primary metric in a key cell: H0 'difference >= 0' rejected by Holm over the 6 key cells
decision_rule.regression: any guard test (start.time_to_start_s, start.ttfb_s, seek.resume_s, start.stall_s in all 13 cells, 52 tests): H0 'difference <= 0' rejected by Holm over the 52 tests; guards cover the swarms without stalled peers (fast, thin, slowlive), the seek and the 1 MiB cell
hard_checks: false bans: app_log.stall_bans == 0 in every fast, thin and slowlive run (no stalled peer there, so every ban is false); a single false ban fails the gate
CW bans at least once in every mixed 4/16 MiB run (otherwise the mechanism did not run and the result is not attributable)
failed runs and tracebacks with an application frame: CW <= C0
pass_if_all: at least 4 of 6 key cells improved

expected_mechanism.mixed 4/16 MiB: Stalled peers hold blocks of the boundary pieces (16 MiB: piece 0 and the last piece, 4 MiB: mostly the last); CW bans them about 2 s after their first request and their blocks go to live peers at once (G0: 16 MiB edges 11.8 -> 6.3 s, 4 MiB 5.8 -> 4.1 s).
expected_mechanism.mixed 1 MiB: G0: piece 0 unaffected, the last piece delayed (4.4 vs 1.8 s); not a key cell because the 1 MiB start already includes several pieces of buffer.
expected_mechanism.fast / thin / slowlive: No stalled peer: CW must not ban anybody and must not change any time.

risks_not_covered_by_the_probe: A live but high-latency or overloaded peer whose first block takes more than 2 s: it would be banned for 120 s. The slowlive profile covers 0.8 s +- 0.4 s; slower first answers stay untested.
Several real peers behind one NAT address: the IP ban removes all of them for 120 s.

A banned peer gets no upload from us either for 120 s (session-wide ip_filter, every torrent). Negligible on a private tracker where the relay is a short-lived leecher, but a behaviour change; documented as the technical default relay_stall_ban_seconds = 120.
Stalled peers that connect after the serving ones (G0 stall_last without watchdog: 16 MiB piece 0 at 20.8 s): the H1 tracker order is not controlled, so this case is only sampled, not targeted.
Peers that recover after a pause (disk stall) are re-admitted only after the ban; the ban list is capped at 64 addresses (further stalled peers stay connected).
A real outage of our own link does not ban anybody (a peer is banned only while another peer of the same torrent progresses); not exercised by H1.
open_questions: Harness ban counter (prerequisite) and the slowlive profile: both new; the slowlive latency is a choice, not derived from real swarms.
Real swarms: the frequency of stalled peers is unknown (implementation plan, SP10 row); a PASS shows the synthetic mechanism, not its real-world prevalence.
Whether 120 s is the right ban length is not measured by this gate (only one value is run); it is a technical default.
